Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Salt Lake City UT
1049 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...


- Strong downslope winds are expected Saturday morning into
  Saturday afternoon across the Castle Country region,
  particularly from around Emery southward through Fremont
  Junction. Wind gusts of up to 50 to 60 mph can be expected for
  this area. 

- A weak storm system will move across northern Utah and southwest
  Wyoming late tonight into Saturday, bringing generally light
  valley rain and mountain snow.

- Dry conditions will return temporarily on Sunday before another
  weak system grazes northern Utah on Monday. A more potent system
  may impact primarily southern Utah for the latter half of the
  upcoming week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...A shortwave trough associated with a deteriorating
atmospheric river will track through Utah and southwest Wyoming
through the overnight hours and into Saturday, bringing generally
light mountain snow and valley rain with periods of moderate
precipitation rates in the Bear River mountains overnight. Breezy
conditions will accompany this shortwave trough, with widespread
gusts of 25-35 mph arriving along, and behind, the associated cold
frontal boundary, mainly across the northeastern half of the
forecast area. While many locations will not see headline worthy
wind gusts, the Castle Country region will see ideal conditions to
support strong downsloping winds along the SR-10 corridor with
peak gusts of up to 50 to 60 mph between 9AM and 2PM. Travel
along SR-10 during this timeframe may become dangerous to high-
profile vehicles. Current model guidance is supportive of the
strongest winds materializing around 11AM to noon, with REFS 90th
percentile wind gusts exceeding 65-70 mph from Emery to Fremont
Junction. Wind headlines for this area will go into effect at 9AM
on Saturday and are set to expire at 2PM as favorable conditions
for strong winds dissipate.

Stabilizing and drying conditions will follow in the wake of this
shortwave trough as a compact ridge of high pressure traverses the
region on Sunday. That said, an active upstream storm track will
help to send shortwave energy back into the region by Monday. A
weak shortwave trough following on the heels of this brief ridge
will track through the region during the day on Monday, with
minimal moisture pairing with the feature. As such, another round
of light, high-elevation snowfall and valley rain can be
anticipated from the Ogden area northward.

Thereafter the focus then shifts toward our next large scale low
pressure system moving into the region as this energy is displaced
from the eastern Pacific. Ensembles remain in good agreement on
this feature pivoting into the southwestern U.S. from Tuesday
through Thursday, bringing potential for moderate to heavy
precipitation across the southern half of the forecast area. That
said, widespread precipitation across the forecast area will still
be in the playing cards as this feature brings widespread moisture
and lift into the region. Due to this low's modification as it
tracks across the subtropical Pacific, temperatures are looking to
be warm enough to favor valley rain and high elevation
(7,500-8,000ft+) snowfall, so major disruptions to travel are not
anticipated at this time. 

After this system clears the area on Thursday, ensemble guidance
maintains an active subtropical Pacific storm track into the
western U.S., providing more opportunity for precipitation across
Utah and southwest Wyoming... potentially looking for our first
opportunity for widespread valley snowfall some time around the
December 7th to 9th timeframe. Time will tell.

&&

.AVIATION...


KSLC... VFR conditions will prevail for the remainder of Friday 
through Saturday morning with CIGS falling below 10kft. Winds are 
currently southeasterly, but will start shifting to become 
northwesterly around 15Z. Wind gusts are also expected to increase 
once the winds become northwesterly with gusts topping out around 25 
kts Saturday afternoon. A cold front will begin to cross over the 
terminal around 12Z Saturday accompanied by rain showers and CIGS 
below 5kft resulting in a 30% chance of MVFR conditions through 15Z. 
The first chance of rain showers will begin around 7z Saturday, but 
the greatest chance of precipitation wont occur until the front 
passes over the terminal around 12-15z. Showers will then quickly 
taper off after 15Z with the rest of Saturday afternoon and evening 
remaining mostly cloudy with gusty northwesterly winds.


REST OF UTAH AND SOUTHWEST WYOMING...VFR conditions prevail for all 
regional terminals through this evening. Expect increasing low-to-
mid level clouds throughout tonight into tomorrow, particularly 
across the northern portion of the airspace. Rain & high elevation 
showers are expected to develop across northern Utah overnight ahead 
of a cold front early/mid Saturday morning, bringing VIS/CIG 
reductions to MVFR at times. No significant weather is expected from 
this system for southern Utah terminals. Most terminals will see 
southerly winds through the day today, with a switch to gusty 
northerly winds behind the frontal passage Saturday morning. Gusts 
will be particularly strong, around 30-45 kts, across southwest 
Wyoming and eastern Utah.
